Jonas — quick question on the commit definition so all managers are consistent: do we count an expansion as a commit when the renewal + expansion are signed together, or only when there is explicit product add-on scope? Example: Acme Cloud is on an annual contract and is negotiating a $60k seat expansion to be billed pro-rata; legal expects a single signature for the renewal + expansion.

If expansions signed at renewal count as commit for ARR, I’ll mark several of our opportunities accordingly. If not, I’ll separate them out and flag for leadership review.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Good question — here’s the commit rubric to standardize worksheets: 

Commit rubric (short):
- Net-new: Contract signed OR PO received with clear effective date (count as commit).
- Expansion at renewal: If the expansion amount is explicitly written and part of the contractual signature (single agreement that includes the expansion line), count it as commit for the renewal quarter.
- Expansion billed later via amendment: Do NOT count as commit until the amendment is signed.
- Conditional discounts / trials: Do NOT count as commit until contract terms are finalized and countersigned.

Practical note: If legal confirms a single signed agreement that includes the expansion line for Acme Cloud, mark as commit. Flag anything ambiguous and I’ll escalate to Sales leadership before Monday’s rollforward cut.

I’ll also upload a short one-pager to the Drive with these rules.

— Jonas
